0.long_answer: Familial hyperaldosteronism type III is a heritable form of primary aldosteronism where mutations in the KCNJ5 gene lead to an abnormal potassium channel function, causing excessive adrenal mineralocorticoid (aldosterone) production. The same gene, KCNJ5, has also been identified in Long QT syndrome 13, where the mutation affects the electrical repolarization in the heart, leading to arrhythmias. Therefore, the KCNJ5 gene plays a dual role in both conditions.
